findings.description: The pronoun "it" in "Run it without the debt flags first" sits closer to the just-named "a plain `pup merge`" (the bad example the sentence warns against) than to the intended antecedent, the `pup merge <task> --pr` command shown in the code block three lines above. A careful reader resolves it correctly via the sentence's own opening ("Always with `--pr`:") and the code block, but the phrasing could be tightened, e.g. "Run the gate without the debt flags first."

"...which opens a pull request where a plain `pup merge` would fast-forward local main (decision 26)..." reads on first pass as if the fast-forward happens inside the pull request, when the intent is contrastive (opens a PR, instead of what a plain `pup merge` would do). Factually accurate once read twice, so this is a wording nit rather than an accuracy issue.

refuted_findings.description: The sentence that splices in the `--pr` caveat introduces 'a plain `pup merge`' as the noun phrase immediately preceding 'Run it without the debt flags first.' Grammatically, the nearest antecedent for 'it' is that just-named 'plain pup merge' — the exact construct the sentence just warned against. The intended antecedent is actually the `pup merge <task> --pr` command shown in the code block three lines above. A misread here would have the agent run `pup merge <task>` without `--pr`, which fast-forwards local main and bypasses the PR/human-review step.
refuted_findings.refutation: The paragraph's opening clause ("Always with `--pr`:") frames "a plain `pup merge`" explicitly as the bad example being warned against, not an instruction to follow, so a competent reader resolves "it" to the command shown in the code block three lines above rather than to the warned-against construct. The harmful misread also requires the agent to simultaneously discard that code block, the sentence's own opening clause, SKILL.md's workflow table ("Always `--pr`: without it the gate fast-forwards local main"), and SKILL.md's separate statement that the human clicks GitHub merge. That chain is too indirect to justify a must-fix-before-merge severity; retagged as a nit.
